summary: Fremont National Forest ground cab built about 1939 in Lake County; removed in the 1960s, and no source describes what remains.

facts.design: 12 by 12 ft non-standard wood ground cab on a rock foundation

corrections.why: The register gives N 43.059920 for the site, at 5,690 ft, which matches the 5,690 ft on firelookout.com. The record's point (43.3266, -121.2154) matches the USGS summit called McCarty Butte at about 5,199 ft (geo.mytopo.com summit 1145921), not the lookout. Human check needed: the Weebly page gives Fremont NF 26S-13E-07, which should be tested against both points.
The register gives W 121.330000 for the site. See the latitude entry for the reasoning; the record's point is about 31 km from the register point.

notes_for_editor: The history is consistent across three sources: a 1939 ground cab, a 1943 lookout appointment, 1948 paint, a 1956 air marking, and removal in the 1960s. The location is the open question. The record's point (43.3266, -121.2154) matches the USGS summit named McCarty Butte at 5,199 ft (geo.mytopo.com, summit 1145921), which is about 490 ft below the lookout's 5,690 ft elevation. The register point (43.059920, -121.330000) matches the 5,690 ft elevation, so it is the likelier site, but the Weebly township reference (26S-13E-07) has not been checked against either point. The record id ends in -2, so another McCarty Butte may exist in the data; check that the id points to this lookout. The FFLOS page credits a 1948 photo (Curtis family, courtesy of Andrea McEvoy and the Ron Kemnow collection); licence unknown, so not added to photos.
